title: whataifound.org registry entry
description: One finding in data/entries.json. Generated from data/vocab.json by scripts/build-schema.py: do not hand-edit. See docs/SCHEMA.md.

title.description: Plain and factual. No hype verbs.

claim.description: One sentence a smart non-expert can read.

field.description: A new value needs a display name in data/vocab.json.

date.description: ISO date the result became public.

verification.description: One of: `formal` machine-checked proof (e.g. Lean); `independent` checked by third parties who were not the authors; `peer-reviewed` published after peer review; `author-verified` verified only by the people who produced it; `claimed` announced, not independently verified; `disputed` substantive public challenge to the result; `known` correct, but the result already existed in the literature; `refuted` shown to be wrong

autonomy.description: One of: `autonomous` the AI did it without human problem-setting or steering; `ai-led` the AI produced the core idea; humans framed or checked it; `collaborative` genuine back-and-forth between AI and human; `ai-assisted` humans led; the AI helped with parts; `search-scaffold` a human-built search harness (FunSearch, AlphaEvolve) with an LLM inside; `retrieval` the AI located an existing result rather than producing a new one

url.description: Must be http(s). Other schemes are rejected by the build.

kind.description: One of: `research` the paper, proof, code or data itself; `announcement` the claim as first made public, by whoever made it; `coverage` news and press reporting on the claim; `commentary` analysis by someone not involved; `challenge` the case against the claim

sources.description: Every link, each labelled with what it is. At least one 'research' source is required for any grade stronger than 'claimed'. Most significant first within a kind.

added.description: ISO date this entry was added to the registry.

humans.description: Named human collaborators on the discovery.

year_posed.description: Year the problem was first posed. Omit if there is no single origin year.

novelty_check.description: What was searched and what turned up. Write it even when clean.

independent_checks.description: What was checked, by whom, and with what outcome.

url.description: Must be http(s). Other schemes are rejected by the build.

discussion.description: Threads where the result was debated. Not a substitute for a source.

videos.description: Credible explainers only. Verify the ID resolves.

name.description: As it should appear as credit.

github.description: Bare handle, no @. Becomes a link. Optional.

handle.description: Their whataifound.org handle, no @. Links to /u/<handle>. Optional.

orcid.description: The identifier that carries weight in a science registry. Optional.

note.description: What they did, e.g. 'verified the Lean proof'.

contributors.description: Who added or corrected this registry entry.

name.description: As it should appear as credit.

github.description: Bare handle, no @. Becomes a link. Optional.

handle.description: Their whataifound.org handle, no @. Links to /u/<handle>. Optional.

orcid.description: The identifier that carries weight in a science registry. Optional.

note.description: What they did, e.g. 'verified the Lean proof'.

reviewers.description: Who independently checked it. Pairs with independent_checks.

registry.description: One of: `mathdb` MathDB; `palomar` Palomar; `proofatlas` ProofAtlas; `vibemathed` vibemathed. A new one goes in the 'registries' map in data/vocab.json.

id.description: The record identifier as that registry issues it, e.g. PALOMAR-2026-08-13-000001.

url.description: The record's own page. Must be http(s).

title.description: The record's own title, when it is more use to a reader than the bare identifier. A MathDB id is a number; the problem's name is what someone is actually looking for. Optional.

repository.description: The repository the registration checked, as owner/name. Optional.

commit.description: Full 40-character commit SHA of the checked snapshot. Anything shorter does not pin it. Optional.

theorems.description: The statements the registration certifies, by their formal names. Worth recording precisely: this is where a claim broader than what was proved becomes visible. Optional.

checked.description: ISO date the registration was made. Optional.

note.description: Anything the record says that the fields above cannot carry, such as a scope limit on what was proved. Optional.

registrations.description: Where else this result is registered and what that registration mechanically guarantees. A machine check of one artifact, not a verdict on the finding: nothing ranks an entry by it, and most of the registry is in fields where no such registry exists.

date.description: ISO date of the edit. Cannot precede the entry's `added`.

kind.description: One of: `regraded` a verification or autonomy grade moved; `check` someone outside the lab checked the result; `challenge` a counterargument was cited; `correction` a factual fix that left the grades alone

note.description: What changed and why, in one sentence. Shown verbatim in the activity feed on the home page.

url.description: What prompted the edit, if there is something to point at. Must be http(s). Optional.

revisions.description: What has been edited on this entry since it was added, newest last. This is where editorial rule 2 is recorded: an entry is downgraded and annotated, never deleted, and a regrade belongs here.
